Can I Edit a Scheduled Post After Scheduling It?
Nothing about a scheduled post is carved in stone. Until the moment Telegram accepts the send, every part of it can change — that is the whole point of keeping a queue instead of posting immediately.
What you can change
Text and formatting
— fix a typo, rewrite the hook, add links. Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoilers and code all survive edits.
— swap the image, replace the video, add or remove an album item.
Send time
— move the post earlier or later, or to another day entirely.
Target channel
— re-point a post to a different connected channel.
Open the
), tap the post, choose
🔄 Replace
. The familiar schedule flow reopens with the post's current content pre-filled — change what you need and confirm.
What editing cannot do
Change a post that already published.
Once the sender bot delivers the message to Telegram, it is a normal Telegram message — edit it with Telegram's own tools, not here.
Edit recurring posts “in place”.
A recurring rule is a single template that fires on its pattern — there are no separate per-day copies. Edit the
rule
so all future sends change.
A workflow that actually works

Channel operators who stay sane usually: schedule the week on Sunday, review the Calendar Monday, and treat edit as the normal verb — improving copy as the news moves. Edits are free, instant, and never notify subscribers. The only deadline is the send time itself.
Common questions
How late can I edit a post?
Any time before the send moment. If the bot is mid-delivery, the edit may not apply — that is the only race. For a post due within seconds, delete and reschedule instead.
Can I edit a post that already went out?
Not from the bot — it is a regular Telegram message now. Telegram itself lets admins edit posted messages in channels; use Telegram for that.
Does editing reset the monthly send counter?
No. The counter counts actual sends, not edits. Editing costs nothing.

How Can I See Views, Reactions and Comments on My Telegram Channel Posts?
Telegram shows view counts under every channel post, but it never shows you
trends

: which topics overperform, what time of day your audience actually reads, which posts collected the most reactions. Fast Scheduler records the metrics of every post it publishes and turns them into dashboards you can browse in seconds.
Where the numbers live
on the bot’s main menu (page 2) or send
. You get:
Usage totals
— lifetime messages sent, messages sent today, and how many schedules and recurring messages are currently active.
Per-channel dashboards
— for every connected channel: average views, comments and reactions per post, plus the top reactions your audience uses.
Leaderboards (Premium)
— your top posts ranked by the metric you pick: Views, Comments, Reactions or Top Commenters. Each board shows 10 entries per page and can be filtered by period (day, week, month, year or all time).
What is counted — and what is not
Statistics are recorded when
Fast Scheduler publishes a post

and Telegram reports back the post’s metrics. Manually posted content that never passed through the bot is deliberately excluded, so the numbers describe your scheduled content honestly. Comments made in the discussion group under a channel post are picked up too, which is what powers the Comments metric and the Top Commenters board.
Three ways to actually use this
Find your format.
Sort by Views for a month: if the top five posts share a pattern (length, media type, topic), schedule more of it.
Time your channel.
Compare identical formats posted at different hours, then move recurring messages toward the winning window — the best posting times guide below has the general playbook.
Watch reactions, not just views.
Views measure reach; reactions and comments measure resonance. A post with half the views but double the reaction rate is usually the better template.

Does Fast Scheduler track posts I publish manually?
No. Only posts published through Fast Scheduler are recorded, which keeps your dashboards focused on your scheduled content strategy.
Are statistics leaderboards free?
Per-channel averages and usage totals are available to everyone. Leaderboards that rank your top posts by views, comments or reactions are part of Premium.
What metrics can leaderboards rank by?
Views, comments, reactions and top commenters — each filterable by day, week, month, year or all time, with up to 50 posts per page.

Free vs Premium: Which Fast Scheduler Plan Fits Your Channel?
Feature tables tell you
what
differs; this tells you
when it matters
. Four questions decide the plan.
1. How many channels do you run?

One channel works great on Free (1 channel, 1 sender bot). Two or three channels — or plans to get there — is the cleanest Premium trigger: Premium pairs 3 channels with 3 sender bots from one account.
2. How much do you post?

Multiply daily posts by 30. Under ~90 sends/month, Free's 100-per-channel cap rarely bites. A 3+/day cadence, or channels where every send counts (news, trading, drops), wants Premium's unlimited sends and queue.
3. Is your content video-heavy?

Free uploads top out at 10 MB with video at up to 25MB, no video in Media Storage, and stronger compression. If your posts live on video, Premium's 100 MB uploads, up to 50MB video, and video-in-storage are not a luxury — they are the workflow.
4. Do you need backups, exports or signatures?
The Export & Backup toolkit (
.fsback
archives, JSON/CSV exports) and auto-signatures are Premium-only. If the queue
your business — client channels, monetized content — backups stop being optional the first time you restructure a month of posts.
The short version
Stay Free
if: one channel, ≤3 posts/day, text-and-photo content, no archive needs.
Go Premium
if: 2–3 channels, 3+ posts/day, video content, recurring automation beyond one rule, or you want backups and signatures.
Either way
: you can start Free and upgrade the moment a limit touches you — nothing you built on Free breaks when Premium ends.
Common questions
Can I try Premium and go back to Free?
Yes. On expiry, limits revert to Free and nothing is deleted — disconnect extra channels if you keep more than one, and the first recurring rule keeps running.
Does Premium change how fast posts send?
Send speed is the same — Telegram delivery does not differ by plan. Premium removes quantity limits and media compression, not latency.

The Best Times to Post in Telegram (and How to Test Them Properly)
“Post at 9:00” advice is usually recycled guesswork. Here is what actually moves the needle on Telegram, plus a testing method you can run with a scheduler in one week.
Windows that generally work
Morning commute
— 8:00–10:00 local time. News, digests, “start of day” content.
Lunch dip
— 12:30–14:00. Light, skimmable posts do well.
Evening prime time
— 19:00–22:00. The strongest window for most channels; long-form and media belong here.
The key word is
local
. If your audience spans zones, anchor to your largest cluster's evening, and let the channel's time zone setting do the conversion for you.
Consistency beats cleverness

Subscribers learn your rhythm. A channel that posts daily at 9:00 trains its audience to show up at 9:00 — measurable in view-rate stability. This is the strongest argument for scheduling (and recurring rules) over manual posting: the schedule becomes a product feature.
How to test slots properly
1. Pick two candidate slots (e.g. 9:00 vs 20:00) and alternate similar content between them for 7–10 days.
2. Compare
views in the first hour
, not totals — that is when your regulars arrive. Fast Scheduler's statistics screen shows view dynamics per post.
3. Keep the winner as a recurring rule, and re-test quarterly. Audiences drift with seasons and habits.
Small things that quietly help
Don't stack posts 5 minutes apart — spacing beats bursts for notification fatigue.
Media posts slightly outperform text-only at equal times in most niches.
Skip the “dump 6 posts at midnight” pattern; Telegram's own limits and your subscribers' patience both prefer a steady drip.
Common questions
Does Telegram show “time of post” that I can use for testing?
Views are timestamped; compare first-hour views across slots. The statistics screen gives you per-post numbers without extra tools.
How many posts per day is healthy?
2–4 for most content channels. Beyond that, watch unsubscribes — the metric that punishes oversharing fastest.

Scheduled Message Didn’t Post? The 6 Real Causes, In Order of Likelihood
When a post misses its slot, the cause is almost always in the delivery chain — the schedule itself is the least likely suspect. Work this list top to bottom; each item fixes the majority of cases.
1. The sender bot lost its admin seat
Someone cleaned up admins and removed your sender bot. Check
Manage Channel → Administrators
: your sender bot must be there with
. Re-add it, and the queue resumes.
2. The token was revoked or replaced
in @BotFather kills the old token everywhere instantly. If the bot shows the sender as disconnected, open
under the bot and paste the fresh token.
3. Permissions were narrowed
Admin exists but without
— a silent killer after permission tightening. Open the admin entry and re-enable posting.
4. The channel changed identity
Username changed or the channel was converted — the old link no longer resolves. Reconnect the channel; schedules are kept.
5. Telegram rate limits on bursts

Telegram throttles aggressive posting bursts channel-wide. If several posts fire close together and one fails, it is usually this. Space posts by minutes, not seconds — the scheduler already does, but third-party bots added to the channel can collide with it.
6. The monthly send cap (Free)
On Free, sends pause at 100 per channel per month until the 1st. The bot warns you before the cap;
shows the counter. Premium lifts the cap entirely.

(status of everything) and check the sender-bot status screen. Still mysterious?
with the channel and the missed time — support can see delivery attempts and will tell you exactly which step failed.
Common questions
Will missed posts send later automatically?
A post that failed delivery is marked failed, not silently retried forever. Fix the underlying cause, then delete it and schedule it again.
How do I know if it was the monthly cap?
The bot notifies you at the cap, and /stats shows monthly usage per channel. If neither shows the cap, it was delivery-side — start the checklist from the top.
